strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company who is responsible for one repeated process and has tried ChatGPT but has no repeatable way of using it at work. Specifically anyone who has written an approval or sign-off step into a process document.
strategy.concept: We wrote a mandatory human check into our own process eleven days ago, built the field that records it, and then never filled it in - so the control existed on paper and nowhere else.

filter.ai_boundary: Automation may prepare the item and queue it for approval. The record that a person actually checked has to be produced by that person's action - it can never be inferred, defaulted or filled in by the system that did the work.
filter.friction: The rule lives in a document, the field lives in the system, and nothing connects them. The work can complete with the box empty, so the box stays empty, and nobody notices until something goes out that should not have.
filter.next_action: Open the place your process document says the check is recorded, and count how many of the last fifty records have it filled in.
filter.process: The sign-off step inside any repeated process - who checks the work before it leaves the building, and where the fact that they checked it is written down. Quotes before they go to a customer, invoices before they are sent, copy before it is published.

strategy.objective: Make the viewer go and count how many of their last fifty records actually carry the sign-off their process document promises, by showing ours turn out to be decorative.
strategy.promise: A two-minute way to find out whether your sign-off step is a control or a preference.
strategy.rationale: Twenty-five of 266 reels prove by authority claim and none admits that the author's own governance did not run. The references supply cadence and framing only: a fixed item shape repeated without variation over a long face take (DbO4zvJR1k8), a reward bookend that makes a long middle tolerable (DZ-wujrTJ0u), an unbroken screen take with live narration (DVaBP3wDAFE), and a forward-to-a-named-role close with its comment gate deleted (DczDlj4qQjI).

title: The approval box we designed and never ticked

traceability.evidence_summary: Our own rules have required a suitability check on every candidate reel since 1 September 2026. The field that records it is filled on 4 rows out of 282, all four on the day the rule was written, and none of the 23 cards drafted since carries it. Three reels on this week's forty-reel shortlist were excluded on content grounds and only one of the three is in the record. The four references contribute cadence and framing: a strict repeated item shape over one long face take (DbO4zvJR1k8, 87.4 saves/1k, robust_z 3.01), a reward bookend that carries a long middle (DZ-wujrTJ0u, 64.9 saves/1k, ungated), an unbroken 60-second screen take narrated live (DVaBP3wDAFE, robust_z 5.0) and a forward-to-a-named-role close with its gate deleted (DczDlj4qQjI, 23.6 shares/1k).
traceability.original_synthesis: Twenty-five of 266 reels prove by authority claim and not one admits that the author's own governance did not run. The rule, the field, the four dated rows and the three content rejections are all ours and queryable from data/radar.db; the fix we chose - make the step block - is stated with the two alternatives we rejected, so the reel is a redesign rather than a confession, and two thirds of the runtime sits on the proof and the redesign rather than on the admission.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would advise 'always keep a human in the loop' and show a stock approval screen. This one shows that we wrote the human into the loop, built the box, and then produced a count of four out of two hundred and eighty-two - and it names the difference between a control and a preference as whether the work can complete without it. The proof is a single unambiguous number on a real screen, which is the cheapest possible thing to shoot and the only visual feature in the corpus that survives creator normalisation on two independent metrics.
